children: Tencent-backed Enflame will debut in Shanghai on September 11 after securing $912 million from its initial public offering. Tencent Holdings (TCEHY), China's gaming, social-media and cloud powerhouse, slipped to $54.80. The valuation picture looks more generous: the stock trades 20.41% below its GF Value estimate of $68.85.

The IPO places an approximately $9.12 billion valuation on Enflame. Tencent will stay its largest shareholder with a 17.95% stakeand the connection runs far deeper than ownership. Tencent generated 83.79% of Enflame's 2025 revenue, making it the startup's financial anchor as well as its strategic backer. Enflame expects nine-month revenue to surge between 326% and 455%, but it still forecasts a loss of 700 million to 860 million yuan.

Tencent's stake will be worth roughly $1.64 billion at the offering price. That barely moves the needle against Tencent's enormous market value, but the strategic payoff could matter more. The listing gives Tencent a publicly traded domestic AI-chip partner while spotlighting the obvious pressure point: Enflame still relies overwhelmingly on the same company that funds it, owns it and buys its products. Tencent's Hong Kong shares separately closed 0.3% lower at HK$434.

title: Tencent Slips Before Its $912 Million AI-Chip Bet Debuts
